analysis.title: Western Union Co. (WU): 3Q26 Key Takeaways: Expect near term rebound as cost savings offset structural compression
key_insights: GS rates WU Sell with an unchanged 12-month price target of $6.50 (~5x P/E on Q5-Q8 estimates) against a $6.59 price, 1.4% downside.
3Q26 was better than expected mainly on margins, helped by faster cost savings plus some timing and one-off items.
Adjusted operating margin was 18% vs 16% Street. Adjusted EPS was $0.42 vs $0.34 consensus.
Revenue was ~$1,009mn, 1% below the Visible Alpha consensus of ~$1,021mn.
GAAP operating income was $131mn (13% margin), 13% below the $150mn consensus (15% margin). Total operating expense was $879mn vs $871mn expected.
Consumer Services revenue was $152mn vs $160mn consensus (5% miss), which GS flags as a near-term risk.
Branded Digital revenue was $274mn, up 8% y/y, with transaction growth of 21%. Retail revenue was $583mn, down 6% y/y.
Management suggested the U.S. business could turn positive. GS stays cautious because the immigration backdrop is uncertain.
GS remains cautious on the structural shift to digital in remittances, which compresses margins and revenue.
Guidance assumes the Intermex deal closes 11/10/2026 (not in GS numbers). Ex-Intermex, 2026 GAAP and adjusted revenue is guided to -2% to -1% y/y.
2026 EPS guidance is $1.28-1.38, both with and without Intermex. GAAP tax rate is guided to 20-22% and adjusted tax rate to 10-12%.
WU paused its share repurchase program to maintain leverage targets. Buybacks were $2mn in 3Q26 vs $52mn in 3Q25.
Free cash flow was $65mn vs $90mn GS estimate, down 69% y/y.
GS raised 2026/27/28 EPS estimates to $1.35/1.35/1.35 from $1.25/1.28/1.28, reflecting guidance, results and the Beyond Efficiency program.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its Sell and $6.50 target (~5x P/E). Cost savings drove the beat, but digital-channel shift keeps compressing margin and revenue.

sector_views.rationale: The shift to digital channels in remittances compresses margins and revenue. Immigration policy adds uncertainty to volumes.

earnings_insights: WU 3Q26 revenue ~$1,009mn reported vs Visible Alpha consensus ~$1,021mn (-1%) and GS est $1,018mn.
WU 3Q26 adjusted (non-GAAP) EPS $0.42 reported vs consensus $0.34 and GS est $0.33. GAAP EPS $0.25 reported vs consensus $0.30 and GS est $0.31.
GAAP operating income $131mn reported (13% margin) vs consensus $150mn (15%). Non-GAAP operating income $178mn (18% margin) vs consensus $160mn (16%).
Adjusted EBITDA $234mn reported vs consensus $213mn and GS est $206mn.
C2C revenue per transaction $11.89 reported vs $11.79 consensus. Transactions were 72mn vs 73mn consensus.
Consumer Services revenue $152mn reported vs consensus $160mn. CMT revenue $857mn vs consensus $862mn.
2026 guidance: ex-Intermex revenue -2% to -1% y/y, EPS $1.28-1.38. GS 2026E EPS is $1.35.
GS 4Q26E EPS (12/26E) is $0.38, followed by $0.30 in 3/27E and $0.32 in 6/27E.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS is uncertain whether or how the immigration backdrop improves over the next year, which affects U.S. remittance volumes.

risk_factors: Weaker than expected Consumer Services growth.
Structural shift to digital channels compresses margins and revenue.
Part of the margin beat came from timing and one-off items.
Share repurchases are paused to hold leverage targets.
Upside risks named by GS: reduced pricing pressure, better macro, neo-bank traction, improved cost structure.
geopolitical: Immigration policy in the U.S. and its effect on remittance volumes.

tension_points.theme: WU margin rebound vs structural compression
tension_points.bull_case: Cost savings accelerated and lifted adjusted margins to 18% vs 16% Street. Management sees potential for the U.S. business to turn positive.
tension_points.bear_case: Part of the beat was timing and one-offs. Digital-channel shift compresses margins and revenue, Consumer Services missed, and the immigration backdrop is uncertain.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Management's U.S. business turning positive or an improved immigration environment would weaken the bear case. Growth ex-Intermex below the guided -2% to -1% would confirm it.
